parsed.explanation: The combined regime stacks traveller-facing exposures at every stage. Entry: the Feb 2025 cable tells officers to refuse any visa case where documents cast doubt on sex, and to weigh a lifetime fraud ineligibility for misrepresenting sex — a universal, state-engineered discovery mechanism; eight governments now advise trans citizens about travel here. Facilities: federal and this division's 2025 law bar identity-congruent use of single-sex spaces in government buildings, with no state nondiscrimination or hate-crime recourse and religious-refusal laws licensing service denials. Detention: federal corrections mandate conversion-therapy practices and immigration custody has documented beatings, forced labour and sexual abuse of trans detainees. Positives (national hate-crime statute, employment ruling, some injunctions, no presentation offence, no police targeting documented) are real but subordinate.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable: refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on applicant's sex; fraud/lifetime-ineligibility consideration for wilful misrepresentation of sex; X markers discontinued; passport confiscation reports; ≥8 foreign advisories issued.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding requires four elements, has limited waivers and is never automatic; several orders enjoined; legal-aid FAQ and ongoing litigation.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry refusal cascades into visa denial/stranding; document discrepancy can also surface at any ID check inside the division, feeding facility and policing encounters.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau adoption (2026) of conversion-therapy policy for trans inmates (hair, hormone removal, psychiatric substitution); immigration custody reports of forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men; trans prisoners no longer counted.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National employment ruling and 2009 hate-crime statute supply only a federal backstop; litigation continues.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained on entry or after a facilities/ID dispute moves directly into these federal custody regimes; state-level 'reasonable accommodation' debate raised solitary confinement for incarcerated trans people.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Division's 2025 law (eff. 1 July 2025) bars identity-congruent use in state schools, colleges and state buildings; federal order bars the same in federally funded single-sex facilities; 21 divisions have some ban, 4 criminalise in circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Trespass-type offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart (elsewhere); 29 divisions plus capital have no mapped ban; private venues largely unaffected here.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Universal exposure for any outed visitor entering state or federal buildings — capitol, courts, universities, parks — with no state remedy to fall back on.

care_services.exposure: Under-18 gender-affirming care banned since 2023 (transitional regime ended 2023); federal orders frame such care as 'mutilation'; DOJ subpoenaed under-19 hospital records; LGBTQ youth lifeline services shut down.
care_services.protection: National employment and hate-crime statutes; a settled state discrimination suit produced an apology and non-discrimination commitment for one programme.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care is not documented as denied, but a travelling family with a trans minor loses medication continuity and risks record exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy targets groups 'radically pro-transgender'; Dec 2025 reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' language; division ranked among worst for anti-trans legislative targeting (2026); religious-refusal laws permit service denial to LGBTQ people.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Rewards memo never lists 'gender ideology' as a reward criterion; counterterrorism text disclaims targeting mere disagreement; no trans presentation offence; no police targeting of trans people documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing lowers the threshold for hostile encounters but has not produced documented street-level police action against visitors here.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division bans under-18 care; state schools apply the facilities ban including off-campus activities; federal order threatens prosecution of teachers facilitating social transition; school environment rules hostile to trans students.
minors_guardians.protection: Nothing traveller-specific documented; national hate-crime statute covers bias violence against minors too.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a trans minor faces care denial, facility exclusion at any state school visited, and potential scrutiny of the minor's documents.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division has no state hate-crime law covering gender identity and no public-accommodations protection; religious-denial statutes license ejections; national bias statistics show persistent anti-LGBTQ hate incidents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling apply; general rule of law functions; no organised targeting, no documented trans killings here.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Assaults can be federally prosecuted, but state investigators lack bias statutes, weakening detection and charging.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No state nondiscrimination or hate-crime coverage; religious-refusal laws unremedied; enforcement of the facilities law in custody unresolved (solitary-confinement prospect raised only in floor debate).
remedies_unknowns.protection: Federal litigation is active: passport suit pending, multiple executive orders enjoined; national equality maps and legal-aid FAQs track changes; one discrimination suit won an apology and $300k.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper federal protections operate, but they do not displace the facilities rule or entry screening; remedies are slow and travellers often depart before they conclude.

anchor_checks.comparison: Closest match: unremedied birth-sex facility exclusion upheld in practice with no visitor exemption. This dossier adds entry-stage refusal and lifetime-fraud exposure plus documented immigration-custody abuse, pushing it slightly below 0.35-A; like it, no presentation offence exists.

Higher anchor: single recurring humiliating screening practice with acknowledged-but-unremedied violations. Our dossier exceeds it with facility bans at two sovereign levels, entry fraud exposure and custody abuse, so it rates materially lower than 0.45.

Lower anchor: birth-sex facility rule plus recurrent police extortion with no remedy. Here there is no documented police extortion or state-street targeting; federal courts have granted partial relief, so the rating sits above 0.25.

Higher anchor: acceptance-based society, dead-letter statute, no universal exclusion. This dossier has an operative universal facility exclusion, entry refusal rules and religious-denial statutes — far more exposure than a mere open question about custody placement.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: visa/entry screening engineered to discover and potentially permanently bar on sex discrepancy, then a division and federal government both barring identity-congruent facility use with no state-level recourse, then federal custody regimes with documented conversion-therapy and abuse if detained, and religious-denial laws licensing service refusals. Discovery probability is deliberately raised by document rules and ID checks; severity peaks at lifetime ineligibility and abusive detention rather than imprisonment for presentation. Countervailing facts — functioning federal courts, partial injunctions, hate-crime and employment protections, no presentation offence, no organised targeting — prevent a severe-risk score but cannot offset tier-1 institutional exposures that operate on every outed visitor. A travelling family adds documented care denial for a trans minor.
